uncited: This family covers specialized voxelization algorithms and data structures that deviate from standard surface or solid filling, targeting specific geometric primitives (lines, porous structures) or optimization constraints (local regions, sparse hierarchies).

It distinguishes itself from the parent [Voxelization](12-voxelization.md) by focusing on non-cubic or non-uniform generation strategies, such as parametric line decomposition, hash-based porosity filtering, and localized spatial queries, rather than uniform grid filling of closed meshes.
The methods in this family share the goal of mapping continuous geometric or logical entities into discrete voxel representations, but they diverge in how the domain is sampled or filtered.
**Definition**: Voxelize a mesh in the region of a cube around a specific point, rather than globally.
The specific techniques described here originate from various open-source graphics libraries and research implementations.
These methods address specific gaps in general-purpose voxelization, such as handling non-closed surfaces, optimizing for sparse data, or accelerating linear primitive rendering.
